blindSummary:
In April 2025 the unit's mayor reaffirmed his commitment to pushing through an anti-LGBT local regulation after a same-sex act at a night entertainment venue went viral; the deputy chair of the local council's law-making body backed it as urgently needed "to preserve moral order and religious norms." This unit is one of eight analysed in an international rights organisation's discriminatory-regulation mapping. No enacted local bylaw with specified penalties yet exists here, and no violence wave or mass police raid against trans people is documented in the dossier.

The active legislative push in a major domestic-tourism gateway raises the probability of future discriminatory enforcement. Elsewhere in the country a regional regulation with articles specifying fines and rehabilitation is already on the books, and a 56-person raid without legal basis has already occurred; here the law is proposed, not enacted, and per the enforcement-over-statute rule the traveller-facing impact is prospective.
blindSourceSummaries: A daily-news site report (27 April 2025): the unit's mayor reaffirms his push for an anti-LGBT regional regulation after a viral same-sex act at a night entertainment venue; the vice-chair of the local council's law-making body says the regulation is urgently needed to safeguard public morals and religious norms, and the council pledges to 'escort' its passage.

An international rights organisation's research on creeping criminalisation maps discriminatory national laws and regional regulations in eight units of the country - this unit among them - documenting how sub-national bylaws criminalise same-sex conduct and gender nonconformity under regional autonomy.
blindTangential: The proposed regulation targets LGBT people broadly; its practical exposure for trans visitors would run through the same moral-order enforcement used in other cities of this unit, if enacted.
